key_insight: UNIEGO learns a richer egocentric video representation by using multiple external teachers as proxies for missing viewpoints, modalities, and foundation-model knowledge. This lets a model trained on first-person video alone capture more of the context needed to understand human actions.
problem_solved: Egocentric videos are inherently incomplete: they come from a single wearable viewpoint and usually a single modality, so they miss important cues that other cameras, sensors, or pretrained models could provide. The paper addresses how to transfer that broader knowledge into a deployable model that still works from egocentric video only.
method: Uses a hierarchical multi-teacher distillation framework, where different proxy teachers provide complementary supervision.
Learns from multiple sources of knowledge across viewpoints, modalities, and foundation model representations.
Trains a unified student representation that can be used at inference time with egocentric video alone.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a practical way to boost egocentric video understanding without needing extra sensors or multiple views at deployment. It can improve action recognition and related downstream tasks while keeping the model usable in real-world wearable-camera settings.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing ego video input flowing into a unified student model with multiple teacher proxies above it.

paper_title: UNIEGO: Proxies as Mediators for Unified Egocentric Video Representation Learning
paper_authors: Wenhao Chi, Arkaprava Sinha, Dominick Reilly, Hieu Le, Srijan Das
